question: In Västervik, how do I report a neighbour who is building without permission or has a badly overgrown plot — who do I contact, and what do I have to write?
key_points: Reports of illegal building or an unkempt plot go to the miljö- och byggnadskontoret, and can be made by phone, letter or email, though the kommun prefers written reports to avoid misunderstandings.

The report should give the property/address, what was built, when it happened, a detailed description with measurements and distances to boundaries, plus photos and a map marking the spot; you cannot report something you merely suspect is being planned.
You may stay anonymous, but if you do you receive neither the decision nor any information about the case — to be anonymous, send a letter without your name and contact details.

Typical reportable matters include building work started without a startbesked, a building put into use before slutbesked, use differing from the building permit, or something built that differs from what was approved.

After more than ten years the plan- och byggnadsnämnden cannot demand correction of illegal building (it is time-barred, not legalised), but the kommun can still act against a plot or structure kept in an unkempt state.

question: I live in Storuman and want to put up a small shed (and maybe a jetty) down by the water — am I allowed to, and what do I have to send in to the kommun and how long does it take?
key_points: Within the protected shoreline zone you may not erect new buildings or change existing ones to a new use, and you may not dig or prepare the ground for such building work.
Marinas, jetties, parking areas and golf courses are named as examples of installations that conflict with the purpose of shoreline protection, so plans of this kind are essentially barred.

It is possible to get permission (dispens) to build, install things or make changes — e.g. for a jetty or a store shed — if you have acceptable reasons and the work does not harm recreation or plants and animals.
You apply for shoreline permission from Storuman kommun, unless the area is also protected as a national park, nature reserve, Natura 2000 site or similar — in that case Länsstyrelsen decides.

You must fill in the kommun's shoreline-permit application form; the form itself lists the additional documents required. The kommun often handles the dispens together with an advance decision (förhandsbesked) on obtaining a building permit, but they take two separate decisions under miljöbalken and plan- och bygglagen respectively.

question: I want to connect my house in Söderköping to the municipal water and sewer network — how do I apply, what do I have to send in, and how long will it take?
key_points: The application (Servisanmälan) for water and sewer connection is submitted through the municipality's e-service, which requires BankID-style login; temporary connections (byggvattenanmälan) are made the same way, and you should consult your VA-installatør about questions in the form you cannot answer.
You must attach a VA-situationsplan (water and sewer site plan) to the application; it can be drawn by hand or with computer assistance.

The site plan must show all outdoor water and sewer pipes plus every building on the property as of the connection date, including downpipes/rainwater handling, drainage pipes and pipes from any wells.

Settle the payment arrangement with a bank or mortgage institution before you submit the application, and use the municipality's calculator for a preliminary estimate of the connection fee (anläggningsavgift).
Once the application is approved, the connection is completed after three months.

question: What happened with the plan for the school area at Aringsås 14:1 in Alvesta — who approved it, did anyone challenge it, and is it now final?
key_points: The plan was handled through the ordinary, standard procedure under the Planning and Building Act (5 cap. 7 section, PBL), not an accelerated one.
The municipal committee (Samhällsbyggnadsnämnden) adopted the plan on 20 March 2025.
The decision was appealed on 17 April 2025, but the Mark- och miljödomstolen rejected the appeal and the plan became legally final on 9 June 2025.
The plan was open for public review from 24 February to 11 March 2025, and incoming comments were answered in the review statement.
Two consultation (samråd) rounds were held — 5 December 2022 to 16 January 2023, and a second one 8 November to 2 December 2024 after the area changed.

question: I Karlskoga I've applied for permission to do work near the shoreline on my property - what happens next, who decides it, how long will I wait, and how long does the permission last once I get it?
key_points: Karlskoga registers the application and sends you a written confirmation of receipt; if no confirmation letter arrives, you must contact the municipality yourself.
During processing the kommun may ask you to supplement the application with missing documents (you get a letter listing them) and may make a site visit to judge whether the work is possible.
The processing time for a shoreline protection dispensation application is not set in the municipal page itself but is governed by the Swedish Administrative Procedure Act (förvaltningslagen).
The decision is made by tillväxt- och tillsynsnämnden in Karlskoga, and everyone who applied is notified when the decision has been taken; the decision is sent to the applicant.

The decision is also sent to länsstyrelsen, which has 3 weeks to decide whether to re-examine ( överpråva) the kommun's decision and may revoke it - and it is your own responsibility to check whether your decision will be re-examined.
The dispensation is valid only if the work has been started within two years and finished within five years of the decision entering into force; after that you must apply for a new dispensation.

question: I own land in Älmhult and I want the kommun to start drawing up a detailed plan (detaljplan) for my area. How do I apply, how long will it take, and what will it cost me?
key_points: Apply for planbesked (planning advisory decision); the application is registered with Kommunstyrelsen and you get a confirmation with a diary number and contact details.
The kommunstyrelsen must decide within four months. A positive planbesked starts a plan process, but gives no guarantee that the detailed plan will be adopted or enter into force.
The handling fee for the planbesked application is 7,000–20,000 SEK including VAT, depending on the plan's scope and complexity.
Whoever signs with e-legitimation becomes responsible for paying the planbesked and the plan fee; a negative decision cannot be appealed.

A separate planavgift is charged (at consultation and at adoption), and any extra studies such as noise, geotechnics or archaeology are paid by the applicant on top of it; a planavtal sets out the cost responsibilities.

question: I own a house in Stenungsund that isn't connected to the sewer — how often does my tank or septic get emptied, who do I contact to book it, and what do I have to do before the truck arrives?
key_points: Emptying is compulsory roughly once a year for every private sewage installation (well, mini treatment plant or closed tank); the number of emptyings is set in the municipality's local waste provisions, and the municipality is responsible for the service.
You may not hire your own contractor: Renova Miljö AB is the municipality's contracted entrepreneur (exceptions can be discussed for really large installations).

For a well or mini treatment plant Renova sends a letter (or e-mail/SMS if you choose) about 2-4 weeks before the planned emptying; if you have a closed tank you must order the emptying yourself or set up a regular schedule with the contact centre.

Access rules the driver checks: manhole lids should weigh no more than 15 kg, a maximum of 15 metres of hose may be pulled (longer costs extra), the road and turning area must take a large heavy truck year-round, cleared and passable, and the trucks must not have to reverse to do the emptying.

Prepare the site: keep the installation accessible and clear of animals and loose objects, remove fences/planting blocking it (no hose through hedges or over fences), mark a hard-to-find well with a stick or flag, and leave the lid unlocked and openable without tools; otherwise a missed-emptying fee is charged and a new time must be booked.

You can apply for a pause (uppehåll) in sludge collection or a dispensation for a longer emptying interval if annual emptying obviously isn't needed — the municipality's environmental unit (miljöenhet) handles these applications via the e-service and a handling fee applies; emergency out-of-hours emptying after 16.30, evenings, weekends and public holidays costs extra and is booked by calling Renova on 031-61 87 75.

question: I own a plot of land in Mark kommun and want to have a detailed plan (detaljplan) drawn up for it — what do I actually have to do, how long will it take, and when can I speak up about the proposal?
key_points: The process starts by submitting an application for planbesked (plan clearance) to bygg- och miljönämnden, which has four months to give a positive or negative answer; a fee is charged according to the taxa, and before planning work begins a planavtal is signed between the applicant and the municipality covering the cost of the detaljplan.

After a positive planbesked the samråd stage collects views: the proposal is posted on the municipality's website, advertised in the local paper and sent to everyone directly affected, normally running for four weeks, with meetings held for larger plans.

The proposal is then put out for granskning (review) for at least three weeks, with documents published on the website and displayed at bygg- och miljöförvaltningen; if the proposal changes a lot after review it must be reviewed again before adoption.
An owner who may want to appeal the later adoption decision must submit comments already during the review period — this is a precondition for mark- och miljödomstolen to allow the appeal.

Bygg- och miljönämnden adopts the plan (kommunfullmäktige must also adopt plans of greater public importance or involving municipal costs); once adopted it is announced, and there are three weeks from the posting date to appeal, after which the plan gains laga kraft, building permits can be applied for, and the whole process normally takes one to two years.

question: We are a landowner group looking to build a cluster of 15-20 small houses in Botkyrka. Where in the kommun would the översiktsplan allow such a project, and what approvals, studies and infrastructure would we need to get it through?
key_points: Single build applications are decided case by case, and the kommun's default is to refuse new housing outside the designated locations.
A project with several properties must go together with a detailed development plan (detaljplan) and an extension of municipal water and sewer.
Where no municipal connections exist, approved private water and wastewater solutions are required.
Suitability is tested against ancient monuments, shoreline protection, power lines, railway noise and valuable nature, and buildings must fit the cultural landscape.

question: A housing group wants to build 15-20 small detached houses with shared outdoor space in Skellefteå. Where in the kommun would a project like this be welcome, and what steps, studies and permits would we need before we could start building?
key_points: The municipal overview plan and its thematic add-ons only guide decisions; a binding detaljplan is what actually regulates what may be built, how big and for what use, and it is the basis for building permission.

If the site is near the shoreline, shore protection applies, but it can be lifted inside the municipality's designated shoreline-development areas when the measure long-term supports employment and the service base of the countryside.
New housing along traffic routes with noise levels of 60-65 dB(A) is only allowed in exceptional cases, and then only with a quiet side, facade sound class B and usable outdoor areas.
Radon risk is no obstacle to planning new housing, but radon-safe construction must be handled during the build stage, and contaminated land from former industry must also be checked.

key_points: New housing should in the first hand be located close to the public transport corridor and stops; localities far from stops are less prioritised for future expansion.
No building rights may be added or enlarged in areas at risk of flooding.
Contiguous agricultural land must not be taken for building where alternative non-agricultural locations exist.

The municipal position at early plan advice and building permit rests on the comprehensive plan's strategies, site-specific conditions and other interests, and the comprehensive plan sets the frame for the detailed development plan that must precede building.

question: We want to set up an eco-village of 15 to 25 homes with shared gardens and a single shared wastewater system, on farmland just outside a village in Upplands Väsby. What are we missing before we can move ahead, and how should we go about making this work?
key_points: Obstacle: New housing on valuable agricultural land in the countryside is restricted, so a 15-25 home scheme on farmland runs into a hard limit.
Obstacle: Municipal policy concentrates growth inside the urban area, strongly limiting any new scattered dwellings on the countryside.
Obstacle: A shared wastewater installation that toilets are connected to requires an individual permit from the municipal committee, which the group must plan for.
Lever: Small-scale new housing in the countryside can still be examined on a small number of sites, if they sit in existing village formations with functioning communication routes.
Lever: Shared facilities serving several properties can be established as a common facility, which suits a single shared wastewater plant for many homes.
Ask: Which existing settlement group and communication route outside the village is the site attached to, and how high is the agricultural land grading there?

question: We want to put up a cluster of six to ten tiny houses on our working farm in the Rättvik countryside and rent them out to young families. Obstacle: A group of 6-10 houses forms a new coherent settlement, which the municipality must examine for suitability through a local plan before building.

Lever: Water and sewer for several houses can be arranged as one shared facility serving multiple properties, which suits a small cluster better than ten separate systems.
Ask: Please tell us whether your farm sits near a lake or river, and whether the ground you have in mind is tilled farmland or already built-up land.

question: We want to convert an old barn or a closed-down village school in the Håbo countryside into 4–8 co-housing apartments for a small group of households. We are not sure what we are missing or what the municipality will expect from us, and we would like to know what could stand in the way and how to move forward with the project. Where should we start?
key_points: Obstacle: Converting an existing building into several dwellings counts as changing the built environment, which the municipality must examine in a coordinated way rather than as a single isolated building project.
Obstacle: Barns and village schools are typically surrounded by productive farmland; such land may only be taken for housing where a genuine societal need exists and no other land suffices.
Obstacle: If the plot lies close to the shore of Mälaren, new or altered buildings can affect shoreline areas valuable for recreation and flora and fauna.

Lever: Håbo's overall plan actively favours new housing in the countryside by filling in village clusters and settlement groups, so a conversion inside an existing village core fits the intended direction.

question: We want to start a market garden on the edge of a village in Mörbylånga, with a large greenhouse, a farm shop and two homes for the growers. What are we missing in our setup, and how do we make the whole thing work?
key_points: Obstacle: Farmland of agricultural value can only be taken for buildings or installations when it is needed for essential public interests and no other land will do — a strong hurdle for putting homes and a greenhouse on worked fields.

Obstacle: The municipality's overarching stance is that total farmland area should stay unchanged and that exploitation should especially be avoided in larger contiguous areas or areas not close to communities.
Obstacle: A separate discharge solution with a flush toilet requires a permit from the kommunstyrelse, so the two homes, greenhouse and shop cannot simply be hooked up informally.

Lever: Farmland area may be kept unchanged provided the change falls under town expansion or development of visitor-based businesses — a farm shop and greenhouse-grown produce aimed at visitors can frame the project that way.

Lever: Where the public sewer network will not reach, individual or shared facilities (gemensamhetsanläggning) are the accepted route for a lasting solution, and the kommun is positive toward forming such shared facilities.
Ask: Ask whether the plot is worked agricultural land and how far it sits from the village's built-up edge, since that decides how the project is assessed.

question: We want to start a small co-housing community of 8–12 households with a shared house and a couple of workshops on a former farm near a lake in Kalix kommun. We are not sure what we are missing at this stage or how to make the idea work on the ground. Could you tell us what we need to check and what route would make this feasible?
key_points: Obstacle: Much of a former farm plot is likely worked farmland, and under the Environmental Code such land may only be taken for buildings if a substantial public interest requires it and no other land can serve instead.

Obstacle: A lake-side location puts the site near shore protection: within a shore protection area no new buildings may be erected, and preparatory digging for such buildings is also covered by the prohibition.
Obstacle: Kalix's overview plan states that new dwellings in the countryside must not be placed so that they hinder the long-term development of farming or forestry.
Lever: Kalix has designated near-water rural development (LIS) areas that are meant to enable attractive housing and facilities close to water and nature, which fits a lakeside community.

Lever: The municipality is the route for testing whether the area suits development: it examines the site's suitability for buildings through a detailed plan, which can also coordinate the shared house and workshops.
Lever: Shared facilities serving several properties can be established as a community facility (gemensamhetsanläggning), a form designed for installations common to more than one property.
Ask: Please tell us how the plot divides today between worked farmland, already built-up farmyard land and shoreline, and whether the shore is wooded or open.

question: We want to set up an eco-village of 15 to 25 homes with shared gardens and one shared wastewater system on farmland just outside a village in Mora. We have a rough idea of the location but no survey, ownership deal or technical investigation yet. What are we missing before we can move ahead, and how should we go about making this work?
key_points: Obstacle: The plot is farmland, and productive agricultural land may only be taken for buildings or installations when that is needed for essential societal interests and cannot be met on other land.
Obstacle: Being inside an area the municipality has flagged for rural development does not remove shoreline protection by itself — it stays until a specific exemption or a detailed plan removes it.
Lever: Inside such flagged areas the municipality has two extra special grounds for granting an exemption, which makes establishing homes and shared activities near water easier.
Obstacle: A group of this size can be handled as one new coherent settlement, which is a case the municipality must examine with a detailed plan covering character, scale and coordination.
Lever: One shared wastewater plant is a recognised community facility serving several properties, a form that exists precisely to serve a common, permanent purpose for multiple holdings.
Ask: Do you already own or hold an option on a specific plot, and how far is it from the nearest stream or lake?

question: We want to set up a cluster of 6–10 tiny houses on our working farm in Strängnäs kommun, out on farmland in the rural parts of the kommun, and rent them to young families. What should we look into first, and what is the sensible route forward for us?
key_points: Obstacle: The farmland your farm sits on is nationally protected: it may only be taken for buildings or facilities under narrow conditions, so a house cluster on productive field is the hardest starting point.
Obstacle: Six to ten rented houses read as a new cohesive settlement, which is exactly the situation where a full plan must be prepared before building.
Obstacle: Each tiny house will need a toilet connection, and a shared facility serving several water toilets requires a permit from the kommun before it can be installed.

Lever: Strängnäs' own planning material points the other way for this kind of site: development there should be aimed at rural dwellings and small businesses, built together as traditional farm or village formations — which suits a small house cluster far better than scattered lots.

Lever: You do not have to start by drawing a plan: you can apply in writing for an early answer describing the main purpose of your intended action, and use that to test feasibility before committing.

Ask: The assistant needs to know where the farm lies — inside or outside the built-up settlement, and how far from a station — since Strängnäs concentrates its growth near the railway stations and only a smaller share goes to the rest of the countryside.

question: We want to turn an old barn or a closed village school in a village in Tierp municipality into 4–8 co-housing apartments, with some shared facilities. What are we missing before we start, and how should we go about making this work in practice?
key_points: Obstacle: If the barn sits on usable farmland, taking it into use for housing is only allowed when societal interests require it and cannot be met on other land.
Obstacle: If the scheme departs from the municipality's översiktsplan, that deviation has to be motivated, so the reuse must fit the plan's direction for the built environment.

Obstacle: Converting an existing school or barn into several dwellings is exactly the situation the rules describe as a settlement that is to be changed or preserved, which points to a collective planning route rather than a single-house solution.
Lever: You can ask the municipality in writing for planbesked early, describing the main purpose and approximate scale of the building, to learn what planning basis is needed.

Lever: In the local dialogue for the översiktsplan, residents stressed that village schools are a lifeline for settlements and a reason people choose to settle there, which supports adaptive reuse of a closed school.

Ask: Ask the user how wastewater is handled at the property today, i.e. whether it is connected to the municipal network or runs its own treatment plant, since this decides the capacity needed for 4–8 flats.

question: We want to turn a working farm in rural Sunne into a small farm-stay destination with six to eight guest cabins served by one shared well and one shared wastewater system. We are not sure what we are missing or how to make the whole arrangement hold together. Where should we start, and what do we need to look into first?
key_points: Obstacle: Farmland of agricultural value can only be taken for buildings if it is needed for essential public interests and no other land will do, so placing cabins on worked fields is tightly restricted.
Obstacle: If any of the cabins, the well or the wastewater facility would end up within a shoreline protection area, new construction is prohibited there.
Obstacle: A wastewater arrangement that toilets are connected to requires a permit, and the application needs drawings, a location map and technical documentation submitted well in advance.

Lever: Farmland may be built on if it is done in a way that takes account of the built structure, the landscape and the site's conditions, so a compact cluster on a suitable part of the farm can be argued for.
Lever: A shared well and shared treatment plant for several plots can be set up as a facility common to multiple properties, which fits the one-system-for-all-cabins model.
Ask: Is the ground you intend to build on actively worked farmland, or is it already built-up farmyard land?
